portal_hypertension.abstract: Diagnostic and prognostic non-invasive fibrosis tests (NITs) are increasingly repurposed to monitor liver disease. However, their reproducibility and the minimal detectable change (MDC, ie, the smallest change that exceeds expected measurement variability) are poorly characterized. We retrospectively assessed variability of blood-based NITs and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient elastography on the same day (repeatability) and across use-cases when metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, fibrosis, or portal hypertension is suspected. portal_hypertension.abstract: Complications in patients with cirrhosis often result from bacterial and bacterial product translocation. This translocation can occur because of portal hypertension, alterations in the gut microbiome, and immune dysregulation. We aimed to re-evaluate admission ascites PMN/mm3 count as a biomarker of 30-day mortality. We identified veterans with cirrhosis using validated ICD-9/10 codes who had a paracentesis ≤24 hours of their index hospitalization in the Veterans Affairs Corporate Data Warehouse from 2009 to 2024. In multivariable analysis, we determined the prognostic significance of ascites PMN/mm3 <100, 100-249, and ≥250. The 4111 veterans who met the inclusion criteria were mostly older...

portal_hypertension.abstract: To characterize primary Sjögren's disease (pSjD) patients with porto-sinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD) and identify associated clinical factors. This retrospective study included 7 biopsy-proven pSjD-PSVD patients and 28 age and sex-matched pSjD controls. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and portal hypertension-related data were collected and compared between the two groups. Univariate logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with PSVD. The pSjD-PSVD group had significantly longer disease duration than controls [59 (36, 180) vs. 15 (12, 69) months, p = 0.031]. portal_hypertension.abstract: Progression of liver cirrhosis is a dynamic transition toward decompensation driven by portal hypertension (PH), while systemic inflammation (SI) mediates organ dysfunction and failure, acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), and short-term mortality. The recent publication of the Baveno VIII consensus and of harmonized organ failure definitions calls for a reassessment of current concepts and recommendations. PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science were searched from April 2026 to September 2026 for consensus documents, randomized trials, and large cohort studies on cirrhosis and its complications. portal_hypertension.abstract: Refractory hydrothorax (RH) significantly impairs quality of life and clinical outcomes in patients with cirrhosis. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) has been suggested as a potential treatment, but evidence is limited. We assessed TIPS effectiveness and impact on survival in patients with RH. Consecutive patients with cirrhosis undergoing TIPS for RH over a 16-year period across 18 European centers were included.
